metadata.document: SUBMISSION ON EXPOSURE DRAFT NATIONAL POLICY STATEMENT FOR INDIGENOUS BIODIVERSITY AND SUPPORTING DRAFT IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

cleaned_body_text: This is the Environmental Defence Society’s (EDS) submission on the Exposure Draft National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity (Exposure NPSIB) and Supporting Draft Implementation Plan. EDS is a not-for-profit, non-government national environmental organisation established in 1971. Biodiversity is being lost at an unprecedented rate globally, and Aotearoa New Zealand is no exception due to habitat loss, fragmentation, and degradation. Aotearoa New Zealand has an accentuated species loss profile due to unique biogeographical conditions and high endemism. Maintaining biodiversity is imperative for protecting ecosystems for their intrinsic worth and for essential ecosystem services. Aotearoa New Zealand is subject to international obligations relating to indigenous biodiversity, including the Convention on Biological Diversity and RAMSAR. Under the RMA, local authorities are required to maintain indigenous biodiversity and protect Significant Natural Areas as a matter of national importance. The Government is reforming the resource management system, introducing the Natural and Built Environments Act, making alignment with the Exposure NPSIB critical. The submission details concerns with definitions, objectives, effects management hierarchies, and implementation provisions across the Exposure NPSIB.
